manifest.deal: Deal before reading on: python3 <SKILL>/scripts/deal.py lemon-3d-model.metadump.json (<SKILL> is the metadump skill's folder) prints your hand, an angle to start from and two deep cuts, and writes a dealt copy: the user's words and don'ts, tier 1 and the review questions, plus a random half of everything else, in a fresh order. Work from that copy: read whole and as stored, this file pulls every session toward the same shape.
how_to_read: 1. Deal first: python3 <SKILL>/scripts/deal.py lemon-3d-model.metadump.json, then read the dealt copy it names for every step below (write-backs go to this file).
2. Read the head: the first 34 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=34, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' lemon-3d-model.metadump.json).
3. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' lemon-3d-model.metadump.json
4. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' lemon-3d-model.metadump.json
5. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' lemon-3d-model.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
6. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' lemon-3d-model.metadump.json returns whole entries.

7. When you have built something that renders, look at it before you finish: python3 <SKILL>/scripts/look.py <your file.html> screenshots it, hovers and opens it, and lists clipping, overlap and overflow. Read the screenshots and fix what you see.

essence.one_sentence: A lemon reads through its outline, its ends and its pitted skin as much as through its yellow: the blossom nipple, the stem end and the oil-gland field carry the read, while the colour shifts across one fruit.
essence.summary: Oblong outline with a blossom nipple; dense oil-gland pitting under a waxy sheen; a peel that shifts from green to yellow; ends that can read matching, varied or damaged.

formula.full: oblong outline + blossom nipple and stem end + oil-gland pitting + waxy soft sheen + green-to-yellow peel shift + faint subsurface rim
formula.essential: oblong with a blossom nipple and a pitted, waxy peel

roles.ends: reads as a grown fruit, not a ball; matching, varied or damaged by reading
roles.colour shift: ripeness and life across one fruit
roles.subsurface rim: light passing just under the skin

angles.text: Start from the outline in grey: an oblong with a nipple at the blossom end and a stem end at the other. Settle whether the ends match, vary or read damaged before any colour goes on.
Start at the peel: many small oil glands pit the whole surface, and a broad soft sheen carries it at render distance.
Start from a cut face: juice-sac segments around a central column, under a pale spongy band just beneath the peel.
Start from the size: about 5 to 10 cm long, with the scene units set before any pit or bump is placed, so the detail reads at real scale.
Start from the look: a photoreal peel with fine pores and a glossy layer over subsurface, or a stylized squat form that reads from a distance.

poles: two ends that match, a regular oval that reads clean
a blossom end and a stem end set apart, or a damaged end, that reads as a grown fruit

tensions.text: fine pitting against the citrus read
poles: dense oil-gland pits that carry the fruit's skin
pits strong enough that the bump reads as sandpaper

tensions.text: real scale against a stylized read
poles: a bold squat form that holds up at small sizes

llm_brief.text: On the table: the user's words “a 3D model of a lemon”, read as one whole fruit with its peel as one object, stem end included, and the readings beside it: a fruit with a leaf and short branch, a cut half, a wedge or slice pair, a stylized low-poly fruit, a print-ready solid, a game asset with levels of detail. Form: an oblong outline with a blossom nipple at one end and a stub, button or short stalk at the other; the two ends can read matching, varied or damaged. Colour, as parts that combine: a pale rind, a yellow body, green at the stem, a darker tip, paler patches, a reddish tone in the underside shadow. Material, as parts that combine: a subsurface base under a thin glossy layer; a sheen from roughness 0.2 (wet, sharp glints) through 0.4 to 0.5 (soft) to 0.7 to 0.8 (chalky); oil glands pitting the whole skin. Build pieces, each a set of options: a subdivided cube shrinkwrapped to a sphere, or a UV sphere whose poles pinch; peel detail as displacement, procedural bump or a pore map; UV seams at the stem ring, the equator, the shadow side or pole to pole; bake, light, camera, background and sampling set-ups; a free citrus node group. Ways in: silhouette first, in grey; close skin, from the pitting and the sheen; a cut half, from the segments under the peel; size first, with units set before detail; the look decided first, photoreal or stylized. Dials, as spreads: length to width 1.1 to 1.2 round-leaning (a different citrus), 1.3 to 1.6 classic oval, 1.6 to 2.0 pointed; length 5 to 10 cm, 6 to 7 typical; scatter 0.5 mm subtle, 1 to 2 mm visible, 4 mm soft; pore bump 0.05 to 1.0 mm, from faint to dimpled. Worn paths, each with its sibling: a perfect ellipsoid beside a tip pushed out with a shoulder band and a stem nub; one flat yellow beside a peel shifting from green at the stem to deep yellow; glossy plastic beside waxy oil-gland skin with a broad soft sheen; a low-poly blob beside edge loops wrapping tip and stem; a painted image on a sphere beside tip and stem built into the mesh; a one-unit lemon beside 5 to 10 cm with the unit set first. Open: the target format and tool (default glTF 2.0 with PBR material); the real size (default about 6 cm long); a render or a mesh, and a photoreal or stylized look, both kept as readings.

ak-lemon-yellow.excluded_sense: the colour alone: a flat yellow swatch or paint name
ak-lemon-yellow.instead: the whole fruit: peel with pores and oil glands, stem end, and form

ak-lemon-other.excluded_sense: a defective used car or faulty product, or a company or brand named Lemon

ak-smooth-ellipsoid.instead: tip pushed out as a sharp nipple, with a shoulder band and a stem nub
ak-smooth-ellipsoid.trigger: a plain ellipsoid is the easiest default for a fruit

ak-flat-yellow.instead: peel that shifts from green at the stem to deep yellow, with paler patches and a darker tip

ak-glossy-plastic.instead: waxy oil-gland skin: a broad soft sheen, pitted glands that catch highlights, rough patches between

ak-blob-mesh.instead: a mesh whose edge loops wrap the tip and stem, with lumps placed along the oil-gland field

ak-cartoon-sticker.instead: a rendered fruit with pore relief, oil-gland pits and a soft specular roll-off, shot close enough to read skin

ak-image-on-sphere.instead: tip and stem built into the mesh, with peel relief as displacement or bump, not a painted image alone

ak-default-scale.instead: about 5 to 10 cm long, with the scene unit set before export

ak-model-sense.excluded_sense: fashion or runway model, statistical or regression model
ak-model-sense.instead: a digital 3D model: the mesh and surface material of one lemon

ak-noise-filler.instead: the visible qualities themselves: pit spacing, sheen width, outline shape, colour shift

k-three-d.text: Is the output a three-dimensional model with geometry and a surface material, rather than a flat picture of a lemon?

test.spec: open the file: it holds a mesh and a material, not a single image plane

k-lemon-read.text: Does the object read as a lemon at a glance, rather than as a ball or a generic fruit?

test.spec: side silhouette: an oblong outline with a nipple at the blossom end

k-end-reading.text: Do the two ends read the way the chosen reading asks, matching, varied or damaged, with the blossom end and the stem end set apart where that reading calls for it?

test.spec: cross-section width 10 percent in from each pole, compared with the chosen reading: matching widths for matching ends, a visible gap for varied ends

k-two-fruit-differ.text: Do two fruit from the same model differ in size and bulge, as real fruit do?

test.spec: render two variants with different seeds; the outlines do not match

k-stem-end.text: Where a stem end is kept, does it read as its own shape, a button or stub, apart from the blossom end?

test.spec: close view of the stem pole: a distinct button, cup or stub is visible

k-colour-shift.text: Does the peel shift from green near the stem toward yellow, rather than sitting at one yellow?

test.spec: sample the peel at the tip, the equator and the stem: three different values

k-colour-range.text: Does the colour range from pale patches near white up to pure yellow, with a reddish tone in the underside shadows?

test.spec: pixel-sample the render: lightest and darkest yellows, and a reddish hue in the shadows

k-gland-pitting.text: Is fine, dense pitting visible over the whole peel, the oil-gland field, at render distance?

test.spec: render distance view: pits resolve across the whole peel, with no bare patch

k-waxy-not-plastic.text: Does the surface read as a waxy skin with a broad soft sheen, rather than glossy plastic?

test.spec: broad soft highlight under diffuse light, tight glints under a hard lamp

k-hard-lamp.text: Under a hard lamp tested at more than one angle, do the pits and lumps still break up the highlight, rather than leaving one smooth white hot spot?

test.spec: hard lamp at each angle tried (raking, mixed and near front); the pit field breaks the highlight at every angle tested

k-scale-metres.text: Is the fruit about 5 to 10 cm long, with the scene unit set to metres before export?

test.spec: longest bounding-box axis between 0.05 and 0.10 units when the units are metres

k-units-up-axis.text: Does the exported file carry metre units, with +Y up and the front facing +Z?

test.spec: inspect the glTF asset: the scene unit and up axis read from the file

k-pbr-values.text: Does the peel material use a non-metal base colour with a fixed reflectance, rather than a metal setting?

test.spec: metallic value 0 on the peel material; the colour sits in the base colour slot

k-uv-poles.text: Is the UV layout free of pinching at the blossom and stem poles, with no stretched islands?

test.spec: UV editor check at both poles: no pinch, no stretched islands

k-detail-aligned.text: Do the lumps and the pores line up with each other, rather than sitting on different scales?

test.spec: bump and displacement preview: pores sit inside the lump field, not across its edges

k-subsurface-rim.text: Does the rim of the peel carry a faint glow where light passes just under the skin?

test.spec: backlit edge view: a soft glow along the silhouette rim

k-bulge-gloss.text: Do the bulges catch a glossier highlight than the pores, rather than the whole peel going glossy?

test.spec: roughness map: bulges sit lower than pits, not one uniform gloss

k-loops-wrap-tip.text: Do the edge loops wrap the tip and stem, rather than making a faceted low-poly blob?

test.spec: wireframe view: loops run along the long axis and gather at both poles

k-relief-geometry.text: Is the peel relief built as geometry, displacement or bump, rather than a painted image on a sphere?

test.spec: the relief shows in raking light, not only in the colour map

k-cut-interior.text: If the model is a cut half, does the pulp read as juice-sac segments around a central column, under a pale spongy band?

test.spec: cut-face view: segment structure and a pale spongy band just under the peel

q-format.text: Target format and tool for the 3D model (glTF 2.0, OBJ, Blender file, STL)
q-format.resolve: ask the user, or infer from the first use

q-scale.impact: scale of pores, bump and oil glands

q-citrus-values.text: The BlenderNation page gives no values, ranges or screenshot for colour, shape, membrane or bump; those numbers come from other sources.
q-citrus-values.impact: colour, shape, membrane and bump settings of the citrus shader
q-citrus-values.resolve: measure a reference fruit or find a source that gives values

prompt._about: The user's prompt, verbatim, split into its clauses. No glosses.

p-request.text: The request: a 3D model of a lemon.

p-3d-model.text: The output is a three-dimensional model.

p-lemon.text: The object modeled is a lemon.

primer._about: Discipline principles that apply to modeling a lemon as one digital object. Inferred principles are the builder's knowledge; researched facts carry their quotes.

prim-form-first.text: Settle the silhouette and proportion of the whole fruit before any surface detail.
behaviors: The tip is the most recognizable silhouette point
Pores and glands only refine a form that already reads at thumbnail size
prim-form-first.principle: Silhouette carries identity at a glance; detail can only refine a shape that already reads.
signals: detail visible before the outline is right

prim-topology-follows-form.text: Edge loops run with the shape along the long axis, and the tip gathers to a clean pole.
behaviors: Loops that follow the form give UVs that unwrap without pinching at the tip
prim-topology-follows-form.principle: The mesh should be built from the shape, so edge flow describes the form rather than fighting it.
signals: stretched UV islands at the tip

prim-pbr-basics.term: PBR base colour, roughness and reflectance
prim-pbr-basics.text: In the glTF metallic-roughness model, a non-metal's base colour is its diffuse colour and its reflectance is fixed.
behaviors: For a non-metal the base colour is the diffuse colour, not the specular colour
Non-metal reflectance cannot be painted, so highlight strength comes from roughness and lighting
prim-pbr-basics.principle: Authoring only what the model varies keeps non-metal surfaces consistent under any light.

prim-scale-units.text: glTF stores linear distances in metres, with +Y up and the front of the asset facing +Z.
behaviors: A lemon at about 6 cm is 0.06 units in a glTF file
Authoring in centimetres without scaling at export gives an asset about 100 times too large
prim-scale-units.principle: Model at real scale so a scene reference (a hand, a spoon) checks it.
signals: fruit looks huge or tiny beside a reference object

prim-common-mistakes.text: The usual failures of CG fruit are a perfect ellipsoid, one flat colour, uniform gloss and detail at the wrong scale.
behaviors: A perfectly symmetric ellipsoid with one flat colour reads as a ball or a toy
Glossy at zero roughness everywhere reads as plastic
Pore detail sized for close-ups tiles or vanishes at render distance
prim-common-mistakes.principle: Real peel varies in colour, spacing and sheen, so one uniform value flattens it.
signals: identical gloss over the whole surface
no colour shift from stem to tip

prim-subsurface-skin.text: Organic skins scatter light just under the surface, so thin edges glow softly.
behaviors: Thin edges and the tip catch warm transmitted light when backlit
A flat opaque shader loses this soft edge
prim-subsurface-skin.principle: Light entering a thin organic layer comes back out nearby, which the eye reads as living surface.
signals: hard, opaque edges on a backlit fruit

lemon._about: The lemon as a 3D object: anatomy, proportions, colour, surface and material values. Lite research; spreads are illustrative, not settings.

lf-colour.text: The peel runs from green through to bright yellow as the fruit ripens, with a yellow-green mix in between.
behaviors: A greener peel reads as underripe, a brighter yellow as ripe
Colour can vary across one fruit, from greener shading to yellow
lf-colour.principle: Colour is a ripeness reading, so it can shift from green to yellow across a single fruit.

lf-interior.text: Under the peel is a white spongy layer, then segments of juice sacs around a central column.
behaviors: The white layer thickens or thins by variety and ripeness
Pulp is about two-thirds of the fruit weight
lf-interior.principle: Interior structure is hidden in a render, but it sets where the peel thickness and the centre read.

lf-peel-surface.text: The peel carries many small oil glands that show as pits or dots and give the aroma.
behaviors: Glands read as small dark specks, so the skin looks textured rather than smooth
Gland density, not gland size, is what varies between citrus fruits
Glands are round pockets; one under a thin skin reads as a dimple with depth
lf-peel-surface.principle: Glands are the surface detail; their spacing sets how pebbled the skin reads.

tokens.note: from a 2025 search snippet, not fetched

build._about: How a lemon model is modeled, shaped, exported and scoped. Methods and readings sit side by side as options with tradeoffs; the default reading is the whole fruit. Only the cited facts are sourced, the rest is the builder's knowledge.

options._about: options, not requirements: modeling methods for the peel and form, each with what it costs and keeps

b-opt-sculpt.text: Sculpt the lumps, tip and stem end by hand on a dense mesh, then retopologise or bake.
behaviors: Sculpting gives the most control over an irregular fruit
A sculpted mesh carries messy topology, so UVs need a clean retopo first
b-opt-sculpt.principle: Sculpting is the most direct route to an unusual shape, at the cost of the most time.
signals: lumps that follow no loop flow

b-opt-subdivide.text: Start from a clean base (cube shrinkwrapped to a sphere, or an ellipsoid), then shape the cage and add a subdivision surface.
behaviors: The subdivision level sets how much smoothing the cage gets
Subdividing a pinched UV-sphere base carries the pinch into the final surface
b-opt-subdivide.principle: Cage-first keeps the form under control while the smooth surface comes from subdivision.
signals: over-soft tip with no loop support

b-opt-displacement.text: Carry pores and lumps in a displacement map on a subdivided mesh, so the surface detail is texture rather than extra geometry.
behaviors: Displacement adds detail at render without a denser base mesh
Displacement needs clean UVs, or it stretches where the layout is poor
b-opt-displacement.principle: Detail as a map is cheap to tune, and it fails loudly where the UVs are bad.
signals: pores that do not line up with lumps

b-opt-procedural.text: Generate the peel pattern in the shader from noise or a height map, with no UVs or sculpted detail needed.
behaviors: A shader-only peel needs no UV layout to look right in a render
A node graph does not survive export as geometry, so it needs baking to images for glTF or a game
b-opt-procedural.principle: Procedural detail is light and tweakable, and it moves the cost into export and baking.

b-opt-lights.text: Light the peel with one of several set-ups, from one hard lamp to a large soft box: each gives the skin a different read, and the set-up is a choice, not a default.
properties: raking key at a low angle
rim light over a dark ground
behaviors: A hard lamp sets sharp shadows in the pits and sharp highlights on the glands
A soft box spreads the sheen and hides the pits
A rim light draws the outline, which carries the asymmetry
Several lights wash out the oil-gland field
b-opt-lights.principle: The light decides which skin detail reads: the pits need a hard source, the sheen needs a soft one.
signals: pits gone flat under a soft box
glands lost in a flood with no key

b-opt-camera.text: Frame the fruit with a long lens from far (flat product read), a standard lens at mid distance, a wide lens close for a scene, or an orthographic top-down view.
properties: wide lens, close to the fruit
behaviors: A long lens flattens the form and hides the asymmetry
A wide lens at close range bends the outline and exaggerates the blossom nipple
An orthographic view reads the outline exactly and loses the sense of depth
b-opt-camera.principle: The lens sets how much of the asymmetry the viewer can see, so it is chosen against the form.

b-opt-background.text: Choose the ground: plain grey or white for a product read, a dark ground for a rim glow, a scene (cloth, table, tree), or a transparent background for export.
behaviors: A plain ground isolates the form and leaves the scale to the viewer
A dark ground makes the faint subsurface rim read
A transparent export needs a shadow catcher or a contact shadow to sit in a scene
b-opt-background.principle: The ground changes what the outline is measured against, so it is a choice made with the light.
signals: fruit floating with no contact shadow
rim lost against a light ground

b-opt-sampling.text: Pick a sample count: low with a denoiser for iteration, high for the final still. Glossy glands and a hard lamp need more samples than the matte peel.
properties: low count with denoiser, for iteration
high count, for the final still
behaviors: A low count shows the glands as noisy speckle
A denoiser smooths the speckle and can smear the finest pits
A high count costs render time roughly in proportion to the samples
b-opt-sampling.principle: Sampling trades noise against time, and the glossy parts cost the most.

b-opt-bake.text: Bake the procedural peel to image maps (base colour, roughness, normal or bump) before glTF export, since a node graph does not survive export. Choose a target size per map.
behaviors: A baked map keeps the look in the file, at the cost of fixed resolution
Target size trades pit sharpness against file size (see bake resolution options)
A bake made before the UVs are final has to be run again
b-opt-bake.principle: Baking freezes the look into images, so it comes last, after the layout and light are settled.
signals: pits soft in the exported file

b-opt-uv-seams.text: Choose where the UV seams fall on a sphere-like fruit: at the stem ring, along the equator, down the shadow side, or as meridians pole to pole. Each trades seam visibility against stretch.
behaviors: A seam through the middle of a pitted peel breaks the line of pits
A seam at the stem ring hides behind the stem nub
Fewer long seams are cheaper to lay out but stretch the pits near them
Meridians put each pole at a seam end instead of the middle of an island
b-opt-uv-seams.principle: The seam belongs where the eye does not travel, away from the pit field.
signals: a line of broken pits along a seam

decisions._about: decision points: each lists the choices and what each costs. The default reading is the whole fruit with the stem end, peel as one object, covering the request as stated. Readings feed the synthesis essence.

d-scope.text: The default is the whole fruit, peel as one object, stem end included. Other readings change the scope of the model.

choices.tradeoff: covers the request as stated; one closed surface
shows pulp segments and albedo; adds an interior and a cut-face material
shows segments clearly; more thin geometry at the rind edge

d-style.text: Photoreal peel carries fine pores and subsurface skin; stylized peel reads from a distance with simpler detail.

choices.tradeoff: fine pores at real scale (0.1 to 0.4 mm pit spread, illustrative); costs detail, render time and careful lighting
cheap and readable at a distance; loses fine pores and gloss variation

d-output.term: render mesh, print solid or game asset
d-output.text: The destination sets the mesh rules: a render needs a clean surface, a print needs a closed solid, a game needs a budget and levels of detail.

choices.tradeoff: open edges tolerated; the export is a viewer or scene file
needs a closed, watertight mesh with wall thickness checked; exported as STL or 3MF
needs a polygon budget, several levels of detail and a baked texture set

d-leaf-branch.text: A leaf and short branch are optional add-ons. They suit a scene shot; they cost little for a close fruit view.

choices.tradeoff: one object; nothing thin to check
thin double-sided geometry or alpha; needs its own material
woody material and a second scale check against the fruit

sc-open-points.text: The article names the method but gives no node settings, colour values, bump scale or stated emphasis, so those come from other sources.
sc-open-points.principle: A process note names the layers; the values that make them read as citrus are not in it.

scr-base-mesh.text: One thread build started from a subdivided cube shrinkwrapped to a sphere, not a UV sphere, and sculpted extra detail at the tips.
properties: subdivided cube shrinkwrapped to a sphere
signals: even displacement with no pole pinch

b-base-mesh.text: Two base meshes appear in the thread: a subdivided cube shrinkwrapped to a sphere, and a UV sphere whose poles pinch.
behaviors: A cube-to-sphere base tends to spread quads evenly across the fruit
Pinching shows at a UV pole once the layout reaches it
Extra tip loops hold the apex when the surface is subdivided
b-base-mesh.principle: Pick a base whose quads already spread evenly, so the detail lands without stretch.

b-export.term: export formats and what they keep
b-export.text: The format decides what survives: glTF 2.0 keeps PBR material and units; OBJ and STL keep shape and lose the material model.
behaviors: glTF keeps metallic-roughness, normal or bump maps and metres, so a viewer reads the peel as authored
OBJ keeps geometry and UVs, and its MTL carries basic colour without the glTF roughness model
STL keeps triangle geometry only, with no colour or UVs in the common form; it suits printing
A procedural node graph does not export as a graph, so bake it to images first
b-export.principle: Choose the format by what the next tool reads, not by what the scene holds.
signals: peel loses its gloss after import
colour missing after an STL round trip

sc-shader-method.text: The article says the artist built the lemon from a procedural Height Map and two shaders, one for the peel and one for the insides.
sc-shader-method.principle: The peel and the interior are set up as two separate surfaces, each with its own shader.
signals: peel and insides as two named materials
surface detail from a height map

b-citrus-node-group.text: A free citrus shader, built entirely from nodes and shipped as one node group to append to your own project; its author lists the adjustable controls.
behaviors: Each listed control is adjusted directly, without tracing the node graph
b-citrus-node-group.principle: A packaged node group keeps the controls in one place, so the look is set without rebuilding the graph.

b-scale.text: Model at real size in metres: a 6 cm fruit is 0.06 units. The 6 cm default is an open question; the length spread runs 5 to 10 cm.
behaviors: Bump depths and gland sizes in millimetres only read right at the fruit's real size
Setting scale before adding displacement keeps the depths in real units
b-scale.principle: Scale sets the size of every pore, gland and bump, so it is fixed first.
signals: fruit that looks large beside a hand or spoon

uv-poles.term: sphere UV unwrap: seams and poles
uv-poles.rung: UV unwrapping for a sphere-like mesh
uv-poles.text: Unwrap cuts the mesh along seams, and the pole option decides how the UVs behave at each pole.
behaviors: The seams set where the surface is opened, so placing them decides where the stretching lands
Pinch sets the UVs together at each pole, so faces meet at one point in UV space
Fan spreads the faces around the pole instead of collapsing them
uv-poles.principle: Seams decide where the cut goes; the pole option decides what the cut looks like at the pinch point.
signals: triangles collapsed at a pole in the UV editor
a wedge of stretched faces at one end

tokens.note: Blender 3.6 manual; newer manuals may differ

bake-procedural-to-image.term: baking a procedural shader to an image
bake-procedural-to-image.text: Cycles can bake shader output into an image texture, which needs a UV map and a margin around the islands.
properties: Image Texture node as bake target
behaviors: The target is the active Image Texture node, so the baked image has to be wired in before the bake runs
A margin fills the pixels next to each island edge, so seams do not show after filtering
bake-procedural-to-image.principle: The baked image replaces the shader, so the bake must cover every UV island with a margin.
signals: dark or blank edges at island borders
a material that goes flat after the bake

bake-resolution-spread.text: Bake size is a spread: small for a background prop, large when close-up pits and pores need to hold.
behaviors: A 512 to 1024 bake reads fine at phone size but blurs pits seen up close
A 2048 to 4096 bake keeps peel pits sharp and costs more memory and export size
bake-resolution-spread.principle: Resolution follows the closest view of the object, not the object's size.
signals: texture file size in the export

tokens.note: no fetched source gives a typical size; the spread is an inference

gltf-base-colour-srgb.term: glTF base colour is sRGB, factors are linear
gltf-base-colour-srgb.text: The glTF base colour texture stores sRGB-encoded values, which a viewer decodes to linear before it multiplies by the factor.
behaviors: A base colour texture baked as linear data reads darker and washed out once a viewer applies sRGB decoding
The baseColorFactor multiplies the decoded linear texel, so a factor is not gamma-corrected
gltf-base-colour-srgb.principle: Bake the base colour in sRGB and keep the factor at white when the texture carries the colour.
signals: colour looks too dark after export
colour shifts when the texture is set to non-colour

tokens.note: Blender's exporter behaviour not verified: the Blender glTF colour-space issue page returned HTTP 403

b-uv-layout.text: How the peel's UVs are laid out for a sphere-like fruit: where the seams fall and how the poles are treated. Each choice trades seam visibility, stretch and render cost; none is the default.
behaviors: Seam placement sets where a line can show on the peel
Pole treatment sets how the pits stretch at the blossom end and the stem end
Even texel density keeps the pits the same size across the fruit
A small pole island keeps the pits round but needs care at the seam
b-uv-layout.principle: Layout is where the detail is spent, so it is chosen against where the eye looks.
signals: pits larger at one end than the other
a seam crossing the middle of the peel

surface._about: Peel surface for a lemon 3D model: oil glands, pores and bump scale, colour and variation, roughness and specular, subsurface scattering, real photos of peel and tip, and how a surface fails under one hard lamp. Built on lemon and shader_controls facts, one 2014 Blender Artists thread (no numbers) and two Wikimedia photos. Tokens are illustrative spreads or photo samples, not settings. Photo hex values are lit pixel samples, not albedo.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where nothing decides it

opt-pitting-method.text: Paint a tileable pore map from a real fruit (the thread's method), use procedural noise bump for an even grain, or sculpt pits as geometry; each trades fidelity for setup and render cost.

opt-gloss-source.text: Drive gloss from the pore map (one texture, pores duller), a separate roughness map (more control), or constant roughness with bump only (flatter sheen).

scr-peel-pores-lumps.term: pores and lumps on the peel
scr-peel-pores-lumps.text: One detailed build in the thread layers two displacement effects: hand-painted pores and random procedural lumps, with the pores inset.
signals: lumps and pores that do not line up

scr-gloss-sss.term: gloss and subsurface on the peel
scr-gloss-sss.text: Forum replies named subsurface scattering with a glossy layer on top as the material's core. The displacement map also drives the gloss mix, so pores take less gloss.
signals: gloss mixed by a displacement mask

scr-colour-range.text: The thread's reference runs from almost white to pure yellow, with a reddish tone in the underside shadows. One poster said oranges need only a different tint to become lemons.
properties: orange shader with a different tint

scr-failures.rung: this model's mesh, UVs and material
scr-failures.text: Replies named missing UVs, bump on generated coordinates, pinching at the UV poles, over-gloss, and lumps and pores that do not line up.

surf-reference-photos.term: real photos of peel and tip
surf-reference-photos.text: The two web photos show peel and a nub at one end, but neither is a close tip shot; use them as look references, and find a blossom-end close-up for the tip.
behaviors: The cut photo gives the pale rind band and pitting, good for a cross-section check
Image 1 is CC BY 2.5 (check ShareAlike); image 2 is CC BY-SA 3.0 or GFDL, so attribution and share-alike follow any texture derived from it

surf-hard-lamp.term: a surface under one hard lamp
surf-hard-lamp.text: Under one hard lamp a surface shows its faults first: pits go dark, lumps break into hard terminators, and over-gloss becomes one white hotspot.
behaviors: A hard lamp turns each pore into a dark pit, so pores that are too deep look like holes
Bump on generated coordinates or a UV-pole pinch shows as a streak under hard light, not soft light
surf-hard-lamp.principle: A hard lamp exaggerates faults that diffuse light hides, so it is a cheap test of the peel.

surf-peel-colour.text: The peel spans a range, not one yellow: almost-white highlights and a pale rind run through pure yellow, green-tinged near the stem, with a reddish tone in the underside shadow.
behaviors: A spread from almost white to pure yellow, green near the stem, reads as real; one flat colour reads as plastic
The underside shadow takes a reddish cast in the reference; a grey shadow side looks off
surf-peel-colour.principle: How colour varies across one fruit matters more than which yellow is picked.

peel_colour_srgb: green-tinged yellow near the stem: pick by eye against scr-colour-range; no sample
#C08501 (photo sample, mixed crate in image 2, mb-photo-palette; not a peel body colour)

surf-roughness-specular.term: roughness and specular on the peel
surf-roughness-specular.text: The sheen is a spread: bulges catch a glossier wax-like highlight, pores go duller, and the gloss can follow the same bump mask.
behaviors: Lower roughness on the bulges gives a waxy shine; higher roughness in the pores keeps them dull
Gloss over the whole fruit was the failure the thread named most often
surf-roughness-specular.principle: The peel reads through its texture and the width of its sheen, not through a mirror.

tokens.specular: fixed at 0.5 in glTF metallic-roughness; the look comes from roughness and the gloss mask
gloss_mask: pore map drives the mix (forum method)
constant roughness, bump only (flatter, even sheen)

surf-oil-glands-pores.term: oil glands, pores and bump scale
surf-oil-glands-pores.text: Fine dense pitting from many small oil glands carries the peel at fruit scale; the bump scale decides citrus or sandpaper.
behaviors: Dense small glands read as pebbling; fewer, larger ones read as dimples
Random lumps over a regular pore grid break the repeat; without them the pitting looks stamped
surf-oil-glands-pores.principle: Pitting at the right scale is the peel's signature; the wrong scale reads as the wrong fruit.

surf-subsurface.text: A subsurface base under a thin glossy layer is what the thread named as the core; the scatter depth sets how much the rim glows.
behaviors: Light enters the rind and leaves nearby, so thin edges look lit from within
Without scatter a lemon tends to read as a hard painted sphere
surf-subsurface.principle: Light that enters the rind and comes out close by is what makes the peel look alive.

tokens.peel_thickness_mm: 2 to 6 (one unfetched snippet); keep scatter inside it

moodboard._about: Two web-found photos (Wikimedia Commons), looked at and pixel-sampled. Seed material to look at and draw on, not requirements. Licences: image 1 is CC BY 2.5 per its file page (check it for ShareAlike); image 2 is CC BY-SA 3.0 or GFDL 1.2+, so attribution and share-alike apply.

mb-ref-cut-whole.term: whole lemon beside two cut halves
mb-ref-cut-whole.text: Three lemons on a pale seamless ground: one whole fruit behind two halves, one cut face turned toward the camera.
signals: pale rind band inside the cut
radial segments around a white core
behaviors: The cut face is paler than the peel: a thick pale band sits between peel and pulp
Pulp segments fan out radially from a central core, so a cut model needs both the segment fan and the rind band to read as lemon

mb-ref-market-pile.text: Dense pile of lemons, mostly yellow with orange-leaning and green-tinged fruit mixed in, under hard warm sun.
behaviors: Peel colour shifts from fruit to fruit, yellow to orange and green at the tips, so one flat colour reads as plastic
Hard sun puts small bright glints on the peel instead of one broad sheen

mb-shared-form.text: Oval body with a short nub at one end, off-centre bulges and a stem button at the other end. No two fruit match.
properties: stem button at the opposite end
behaviors: A perfect ellipsoid reads as a generic fruit or an egg; the nub and bulges carry the lemon identity

mb-shared-surface.text: Fine dense pitting over the whole peel, with a broad soft sheen under diffuse light and tight glints under hard light.
behaviors: The pitting stays visible at fruit scale, so pore-scale bump or displacement carries the peel look
Under diffuse light the highlight is wide and soft; under hard light it breaks into small glints. The light changes the highlight, not the material
mb-shared-surface.principle: The peel reads through its texture and the width of its sheen, not through a mirror reflection.

mb-light-context.text: Soft even light on a white ground for the cut halves; hard warm sun on the crate, with bright glints and deep gaps between fruit.
behaviors: The white ground lifts the underside and rims of the fruit, so the form reads without a dark backdrop
Hard sun pushes shadow into the gaps between fruit, which separates overlapping forms
signals: soft shadow under the cut halves
hard glints and dark gaps in the crate

mb-photo-palette.text: Pixel-sampled colours from the two photos: peel yellows and ambers, a pale rind, and a white backdrop. Shares are of the whole image, backdrop included.

form._about: Lemon form for a 3D model: silhouette, proportions, the blossom tip, the stem end and calyx, and the readings a symmetric or irregular form can take. Several shapes are readings of a lemon, none the default. Proportion and tip figures are illustrative spreads from unfetched snippets, not settings.

variations._about: Shape variations far apart, each with what it does. Labelled as readings of the form, not as the lemon. Ratios are illustrative spreads.

var-pointed.text: Elongated, with a pronounced blossom point; the tip becomes a feature of the silhouette.
behaviors: The tip is now a strong cue, so check the pole mesh and the UVs there

var-round.text: Rounder and thicker in profile, with a blunt blossom end and little taper; reads as a different citrus.
behaviors: Pulls the reading toward an orange or mandarin as the ratio drops toward 1.1

var-stylized.text: A near-symmetric oval with a bold, simple tip and a crisp outline, simplified for graphic or game looks; it trades botanical detail for a clean read.
behaviors: The clean outline holds up at small sizes
Gives up botanical accuracy, so the peel detail is simplified to match

var-damaged-asymmetric.text: A lemon with a flattened side, a bent axis, or a dented or bruised end: an irregular reading that suggests growth, handling or damage.
behaviors: A mild asymmetry reads as grown fruit; a strong one reads as damaged, which may be the wanted story or not
Dents and flats need a matching shading change, or they look like a modelling error
The most irregular silhouette here, so the pole and UV checks matter more

var-classic-oval.text: An oval with a blossom nipple and a tapered stem end: one common lemon reading, one of several.
behaviors: Reads as a lemon at a glance in most looks

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where nothing in the prompt decides the form

opt-stem-presence.text: Stalk stub and calyx kept, or the stalk removed to a flat button: the stalk adds a small silhouette break and a ring of detail; a flat button keeps the pole clean for UVs.
behaviors: A stalk stub is the single extra silhouette break; removing it leaves a cleaner pole for the mesh

opt-break-ellipsoid.text: Ways to move from a regular form toward an irregular one: a lattice pull on one end, low-frequency displacement over the whole form, or a slight flat along one side. Leaving the form symmetric is also an option.
behaviors: Lattice pull changes the silhouette most; low-frequency displacement changes it least but adds lumps; side flattening adds a believable bulk asymmetry

form-proportions.text: Length to width sits in a band rather than at one number; where in the band it lands sets whether the fruit reads as a lemon or as a rounder citrus.
behaviors: A ratio near 1.0 reads round, closer to an orange
A ratio near 1.5 reads as the classic lemon oval
Pushed past about 1.8 the fruit reads as elongated or pointed
Absolute size changes the detail scale, not the reading
form-proportions.principle: Ratio decides the reading more than size does.
signals: length over width in side view

tokens.note: The research snippet gave 5 to 10 cm and 1.3 to 1.6 from two samples; no fetched source measured the fruit. Read these as spreads.

form-apex-tip.text: A small nipple at the blossom pole: a bump rather than a spike, and its size runs from barely there to a clear point.
behaviors: A tip that grows past a few millimetres tends to read as a point or a cone
A tip with no proper mesh pole pinches the shading and the UVs at that pole
The tip is usually the first cue for which way up the fruit is
form-apex-tip.principle: A small tip gives orientation; a large one changes the species reading.
signals: stretched UV island at the tip

tokens.note: No fetched source confirms the tip. The research figure of 1 to 3 mm came from an unfetched snippet.

form-stem-end.text: The narrower pole: a shallow cup holding a calyx ring and either a short stalk stub or a plain button where the stalk is gone.
behaviors: A stalk stub breaks the silhouette at that pole; no stalk leaves a clean dimple
A calyx ring reads as a ridge in the shading, so it wants a small crease or bump rather than a colour change
The stem end often carries the greener tint of a ripening fruit
form-stem-end.principle: The stem end and tip sit at opposite poles, so the two small breaks tell orientation both ways.
signals: stalk stub at the narrow pole
ring in the shading at the cup
green tint at the stem end

tokens.note: No fetched source gives calyx or cup dimensions. Spreads only.

lemon-ratio-leads.text: Length to width figures seen only in search snippets: a lemon cultivar description gives about 1.7, and a Verna lemon shape-index study exists but its values were not retrieved.
behaviors: A 1.7 ratio reads as clearly elongated; a 1.3 to 1.6 range reads as a typical lemon
lemon-ratio-leads.principle: A single cultivar figure is a lead, not a measured lemon ratio.
signals: blossom end narrower than a round fruit

tokens.note: not fetched; the USPTO patent and the AGRIS record were not read in full (AGRIS blocked by robots)

form-ellipsoid-failure.text: A symmetric ellipsoid with even ends is one reading of the lemon: a ball, an egg or a toy in plain looks, a regular clean fruit in graphic ones. Compare the round, pointed and classic oval shapes in the variations.
behaviors: With one flat colour and no peel detail, it reads as a ball or a toy
With gland detail and a graphic look, it reads as a clean lemon
A light outline asymmetry tends to read as grown fruit; it is one option, not a rule
form-ellipsoid-failure.principle: Symmetry is a choice of reading: regular forms read as made or stylised, irregular ones as grown or handled.
never_implies: Symmetry is not a fault; an even-ended lemon is a valid reading

form-silhouette.text: An oblong to ovoid outline. Whether its two ends differ is one reading: a rounder blossom end with a narrower stem end reads as the classic lemon, while matching ends read as a regular oval (see the symmetric ellipsoid reading).
behaviors: Differing end widths tend to read as a lemon; matching ends read as a regular oval or an egg, a choice of reading rather than an error
If the differing-ends reading is chosen, the blossom end carries most of the width change, so check it first in the outline
An outline that reads at thumbnail size settles the reading before any peel detail shows
form-silhouette.principle: The outline carries the reading at a glance; the same outline can be read as a lemon, an egg or a ball depending on the ends.
signals: one blunt end in side view
two matching ends in side view

vocabulary._about: Seed words and associations around the lemon and the 3D model. Inferred, tier 2 to 4: they widen the search and never define the task. Senses are resolved in anti_keywords.

lx-cg-vocab.text: The domain's own words for building the peel: base colour, roughness, bump or displacement, and subsurface.
behaviors: Bump on generated coordinates slides when the mesh is edited
Subdivision level sets how fine a bump can read
lx-cg-vocab.principle: Shape comes from the mesh, pores from the normal or bump, colour from the base map.

lx-deep-cuts.term: deep cuts: citrus relatives and near forms
lx-deep-cuts.text: Close citrus relatives that show what a lemon is not: its ratio, its pith, its tips.
properties: Meyer: rounder, thinner peel, deeper yellow
behaviors: A rounder outline than a lemon's reads as a Meyer or a lime, not a lemon
A thick pale pith under the peel reads as a citron
lx-deep-cuts.principle: Relatives sharpen the lemon by showing its ratio and its tips, which carry the silhouette.

lx-descriptors.text: People call a lemon oblong, pebbled and waxy, bright and sharp, with nipple-like ends and an oily, zesty smell.
behaviors: Pebbled and dimpled name the same pits at two scales
A waxy sheen reads as a thin oily film on the peel
lx-descriptors.principle: Plain words describe the look; technical words name the layer under it.

lx-influences.text: Lineages whose habits transfer to a lemon model, each with what it contributes. Contributions, not styles to copy.
contribution: Dutch still life: specular highlights on fruit, the peel as a glossy surface
Spanish bodegon: hard raking light against a matte ground
Food product photography: even light with controlled highlights
Botanical illustration: profile views, stem and leaf read as part of the form
Photoscanned citrus: real pore and oil-gland detail as a check on the bump
behaviors: A single soft key light on a dark ground makes pores and dimples readable
Botanical illustration keeps the stem and leaf in profile
lx-influences.principle: The still-life tradition treats the fruit as a surface to light, not a shape to draw.
